Installing drawbridge

One of two paths, depending on whether your device's setup wizard offers a QR scanner.

The standard way: QR code

  1. 1
    Start from a fresh device, or do a factory reset. Back up your data first, since a reset wipes it.
  2. 2
    On the welcome screen, tap the same spot 6 times to reveal a hidden QR scanner.
  3. 3
    Scan the drawbridge QR code.
  4. 4
    Wait for setup to finish — the device downloads, verifies and installs everything on its own.

If the QR code doesn't work

Some devices ship a setup wizard without the six-tap gesture, or skip the QR scanner entirely. There is a second way in, over USB, that works regardless.

  1. 1
    Continue through setup, but don't sign in to any account — skip that step. This matters: the installer needs a device with no account yet configured.
  2. 2
    Enable Developer Options (tap the build number in Settings → About phone several times) and turn on USB debugging.
  3. 3
    Connect your device to a computer with a USB cable, and use the installer below.
  4. 4
    Wait for setup to finish.
Browser-based installer — coming soon

A page here will let you install drawbridge straight from a Chromium-based browser (Chrome, Edge) over USB — no separate software to install. It isn't ready yet.

Install over USB — coming soon

In the meantime, technically comfortable users can grant drawbridge the same access using Android's own adb developer tool from a computer, on a device with no account signed in yet.

After setup

  1. 5
    Open the drawbridge app and activate it.
  2. 6
    Write down the deactivation code shown once — or don't, if you want the protection to stay on for good.

Read the Q&A for what's blocked and why, or see the full sourced breakdown.
